items.title: NGOs call on PM to tackle inequality amid North Sea drilling rumours
items.summary: Almost 100 charity leaders, including from Oxfam, ActionAid and WaterAid, have urged Prime Minister (PM) Andy Burnham to help address the root causes of poverty, including climate change.

items.title: Getting ahead: Five ways to future-proof supply chains
items.summary: From climate shocks and water scarcity to geopolitical tensions and resource constraints, supply chain disruption has become a defining business risk.

items.title: Fossil fuel giants to double profits as emissions spike, research finds
items.summary: Fossil fuel firms including BP, Chevron, and Shell are expected to double their combined net income to $45bn this quarter, with research stating that emissions from the world’s largest oil and gas businesses were sufficient to cause one quarter of heatwaves experienced in the last 20 years.

items.title: Indigenous leaders present UN with roadmap to protect communities
items.summary: At the latest session of the Expert Mechanism on the rights of Indigenous Peoples (EMRIP), members proposed a 12-step plan to help protect Indigenous communities from mounting threats.

items.title: Ed Miliband to lead UK engagement at World Bank on climate and development
items.summary: The UK Government has announced that the Foreign Secretary, Ed Miliband, will take on the role of UK Governor to the World Bank, taking personal leadership of the UK’s engagement on international development and climate finance.

items.title: What do the Government’s new drought plans mean for businesses?
items.summary: Drought has been declared in parts of the UK for the first time this year as hosepipe bans spread and water shortages intensify.
